verdict.rationale: Make documents first-party Skills that help an AI assistant build scenarios and configure modules, and its official MCP server lets AI clients such as Claude and ChatGPT view and modify scenarios. Together these let a user create or edit a workflow from a natural-language prompt, but only through an external AI client; the pack shows no native prompt-to-scenario builder inside Make. Missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language scenario generator or editor, depth evidence on how well prompt-built scenarios turn out, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can generate or edit a workflow from a natural-language prompt

citations.quote: Make Skills are Markdown files that help your assistant reliably perform Make-specific tasks, including building scenarios, configuring modules
View and modify scenarios and their related entities (e.g., connections, webhooks, and data stores)
Make MCP server allows AI systems, such as large language models (LLMs), to run scenarios and manage the contents of your Make account.
